title: Reinforcement Learning and PK-PD Models Integration to Personalize the Adaptive Dosing Protocol of Erdafitinib in Patients With Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma

content.abstract_summary: Introduces and evaluates a Q-learning (QL) + PK-PD framework for individual-level personalization of the erdafitinib adaptive dosing protocol in metastatic urothelial carcinoma. Erdafitinib is an FDA-approved FGFR inhibitor whose dosing is guided by serum phosphate [PO4]serum — a dual biomarker of efficacy (≥5.5 mg/dL) and toxicity (<7 mg/dL). The MDP is formulated with 86 states (L_PO4 × D_P × L_int), 5 dose levels (4, 5, 6, 8, 9 mg/day), and a manually designed reward function. A personal QL agent is trained for each of 141 virtual patients (96 completely + 45 partially responsive) using the patient's PK-PD model as a digital twin. QL-agents outperform the FDA-approved protocol at every clinical timepoint, achieving 97.87% vs. 70.21% in the efficacy range at month 4, and completely eliminating severe hyperphosphatemia events. The companion paper de_carlo_2025 extends this framework to a 3-biomarker multiobjective dosing problem.
key_findings: The erdafitinib case study is formalized as an MDP with 86 states (combining [PO4]serum discretized in 6 levels, previous dose, and hyperphosphatemia interruption flag), 5 dose levels as actions, and a piecewise reward function (β1=10 for biomarker level, β2=5 for % of days in target range)
At 2 weeks: QL agents had 76.59% of patients in efficacy range vs. 34.05% for clinical protocol; 0% vs. 15.60% in severe hyperphosphatemia — largest relative gap across all timepoints
At end of month 4 (median time for assessing erdafitinib efficacy): QL 97.87% vs. clinical 70.21% in efficacy range; severe hyperphosphatemia: 0% vs. 0% (both)
At end of treatment (5 months): QL 68.09% vs. clinical 56.73% in efficacy (all patients); in completely responsive subgroup: QL 100% vs. clinical 83.33%
Severe hyperphosphatemia completely eliminated by QL agents throughout the full 5-month treatment; moderate hyperphosphatemia drastically reduced

Personalization of the starting dose is key: QL agents chose the clinical starting dose of 8 mg/day in only 23.40% of patients — lower starting doses were preferred in most patients to avoid early toxicity
Population QL (one-for-all agent trained on all 141 patients) performed worse than personalized QL agents — confirms that individual-level optimization is necessary for heterogeneous populations
Completely and partially responsive patients (96 vs. 45) behave differently — the stratified virtual population design is essential to test framework flexibility across IIV
limitations: RUV not considered — assumes PK-PD model perfectly describes pharmacological response; adding RUV may require switching from MDP to POMDP or from QL to stochastic RL variants
Individual PK-PD parameters assumed fully known from treatment start — in practice, Bayesian online learning must progressively estimate these from monitoring observations
Only validated on virtual patients derived from a published PopPK-PD model — no real-world clinical data
Reward function and action set designed by modelers based on literature knowledge; reward function design should be reviewed with clinicians before clinical translation
A completely different action set or freedom level could change results — the arbitrary design choices in MDP formulation are a key limitation of all RL dosing frameworks

extracted_claims.text: "QL agents outperform the approved dose-adaptive rules, increasing more than 10% the efficacy and the safety of treatment at each end point."

"At each of the three timepoints, the QL-based individual protocols resulted in a higher percentage of patients with [PO4]serum in the efficacy range and in a lower percentage of subjects in hyperphosphatemia then the clinical one."

"The personalization of the initial dose significantly increased QL-agent performances. As reported in Figure 4e, the clinical initial dose of 8mg/day was selected by the QL-agents only in 23.40% of patients, whereas the lower starting doses were generally preferred."

"In view of an actual clinical application, the design of the reward function, as well as the entire formalization of the proposed RL-framework, should be carefully reviewed with clinicians to ensure that all the key aspects of the erdafitinib treatment are correctly considered and modeled."

gaps_addressed: Provides the first complete MDP formulation for a real FDA-approved oncology dose-adaptive protocol (erdafitinib) — establishes the state/action/reward design methodology that de_carlo_2025 then extends to 3 biomarkers

The 86-state MDP, reward function (piecewise, two-term), and digital patient twin paradigm are the technical building blocks the WG needs to critically analyze and improve with mathematical rigor (Pillar 3)
The 23.40% adoption of clinical starting dose is a striking empirical result that validates individual-level optimization — directly motivates the WG's position on RL vs. one-size-fits-all protocols
